claim: Promptfoo is a TypeScript/MIT-licensed eval tool with ~22.0k GitHub stars as of June 2026, used by OpenAI and Anthropic, covering prompt/agent/RAG testing plus red teaming with declarative configs and CI/CD integration.
quote: Test your prompts, agents, and RAGs. Red teaming/pentesting/vulnerability scanning for AI. Compare performance of GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and more. Simple declarative configs with command line and CI/CD integration.  Used by OpenAI and Anthropic.

claim: DeepEval (confident-ai) is a Python/Apache-2.0 LLM evaluation framework with ~16.0k GitHub stars as of June 2026.
Inspect (UK AISI, repo UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai) is a Python/MIT framework for large language model evaluations with ~2.2k GitHub stars as of June 2026.
quote: Inspect: A framework for large language model evaluations

claim: OpenAI Evals is a Python framework and open-source benchmark registry with ~18.6k GitHub stars, but its last push was April 2026 (slower maintenance cadence) and it carries a custom (NOASSERTION) license.
quote: Evals is a framework for evaluating LLMs and LLM systems, and an open-source registry of benchmarks.

claim: Ragas (transferred from explodinggradients to vibrantlabsai/ragas) is a Python/Apache-2.0 RAG-focused eval library with ~14.3k stars, though its last push (Feb 2026) lags more actively maintained peers.
quote: full: vibrantlabsai/ragas | stars: 14306 | lang: Python | license: Apache-2.0 | pushed: 2026-02-24

claim: EleutherAI's lm-evaluation-harness is a Python/MIT framework for few-shot benchmark evaluation of language models with ~12.9k stars, the de-facto standard for academic model benchmarking.
quote: A framework for few-shot evaluation of language models.

claim: TruLens (truera/trulens) is a Python/MIT evaluation and tracking library for LLM experiments and AI agents with ~3.4k stars as of June 2026.
quote: Evaluation and Tracking for LLM Experiments and AI Agents

claim: UpTrain offers 20+ preconfigured checks for language/code/embedding use cases but appears stalled, with its last GitHub push in August 2024 (~2.4k stars).
quote: We provide grades for 20+ preconfigured checks (covering language, code, embedding use-cases) ... pushed: 2024-08-18

claim: Langfuse, an open-source AI engineering platform bundling LLM evals with observability, metrics, prompt management and datasets, leads adjacent traction at ~28.8k stars.
quote: Open source AI engineering platform: LLM evals, observability, metrics, prompt management, playground, datasets. Integrates with OpenTelemetry, LangChain, OpenAI SDK, LiteLLM, and more.

claim: Arize Phoenix provides AI observability and evaluation with ~10.1k GitHub stars, positioning it among the larger eval/observability hybrids.

Across the three leading testing tools, Promptfoo (Node.js/CLI, YAML) ships 50+ assertions and 40+ red-team categories, DeepEval (Python/pytest) ships 14+ metrics, and Ragas (Python library) ships 8 core RAG metrics; all three are free OSS with only Promptfoo and DeepEval offering paid hosted/enterprise tiers.
quote: Promptfoo: Node.js / CLI (YAML config) ... 50+ assertions, 40+ red-team categories | DeepEval: Python (pytest) ... 14+ metrics (RAG, bias, hallucination) | RAGAS: Python (library) ... 8 core RAG metrics

claim: DeepEval runs metrics such as G-Eval, task completion, answer relevancy, faithfulness, and hallucination using LLM-as-a-judge with chain-of-thought, plus local NLP models, framed as a Pytest-like unit-testing experience for LLM outputs.
quote: metrics such as G-Eval, task completion, answer relevancy, hallucination, etc., which uses LLM-as-a-judge and other NLP models that run locally on your machine

claim: DeepEval ships purpose-built metrics including FaithfulnessMetric, AnswerRelevancyMetric, BiasMetric, ToxicityMetric, SummarizationMetric and ToolCorrectnessMetric, while Ragas offers the deepest RAG metric set (faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision/recall, context utilization, noise sensitivity).
quote: DeepEval has more purpose-built evaluation metrics (14+) including FaithfulnessMetric, AnswerRelevancyMetric, BiasMetric, ToxicityMetric, SummarizationMetric, and ToolCorrectnessMetric

claim: Inspect AI structures evals around tasks, datasets, solvers and scorers, and in 2026 supports agent evaluations with a built-in ReAct agent, multi-agent primitives, bridges to external agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI), and Docker/Kubernetes/Modal sandboxing for untrusted model code.
quote: Components are the building blocks of an evaluation: tasks, datasets, solvers, and scorers ... Support for agent evaluations, including flexible built-in agents, multi-agent primitives, and the ability to run arbitrary external agents like Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI

claim: Practitioners describe Inspect AI (UK AISI) as a serious, well-architected Python library for LLM evals, attractive for reproducible and security/safety-oriented evaluation work rather than quick prompt iteration.
quote: Inspect AI, An OSS Python Library For LLM Evals

claim: Operator consensus in 2026 is that mature teams converge on two tools: a lightweight CI/CD-gating framework (DeepEval, Ragas, or Promptfoo) paired with a platform for human annotation and dashboards, and that the real recurring cost is LLM-judge API tokens (~$150-$500/month at 10,000 evals/day).
quote: Experienced teams keep converging on needing two tools: a lightweight framework for CI/CD gating ... the real cost is LLM judge API tokens—at 10,000 evaluations per day this is $150-$500 per month in judge tokens
